stops.name: Belva crater
stops.text: An impact crater about 0.9 km across on the delta. Marker is at the IAU catalogue centre (18.48°N, 77.38°E), which is given to 0.01° (about 600 m), so treat the position as approximate.
stops.source: IAU / USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Feature 15872

stops.name: Delta front scarp
stops.kind: Observation from our terrain data + NASA context
stops.text: The steepest ground the direct route crosses (22.0° in our slope grid). NASA describes the landform here as an ancient river delta, evidence that a lake once filled Jezero Crater.
stops.source: Slope: HiRISE DTM DTEEC_002387_1985_003798_1985_A01. Context: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 landing press kit

context.text: Jezero is an IAU-named crater 47.5 km across, centred at 18.41°N, 77.69°E. The study area lies inside its western part.

NASA's Perseverance rover landed in Jezero Crater on 18 February 2021. NASA reports the nearest delta remnant was about 2.3 km west of the landing site. Our start point is a chosen point on the crater floor, not the landing site.
context.source: NASA Science: Perseverance view of the delta
